t:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 300 Vine Street in New Lenox, Illinois, shall be known and designated as the “Jacob M. Lowell Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Jacob M. Lowell Post Office Building”.

fable.w: This section only names a post office building and directs that existing references in federal records be read as references to the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but here it appears only in boilerplate listing kinds of records, not as authority to issue rules. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Jacob M. Lowell Post Office Building”.

qwen_block.w: This section simply designates a name for a federal facility and updates references to it. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_block.s:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 300 Vine Street in New Lenox, Illinois, shall be known and designated as the “Jacob M. Lowell Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Jacob M. Lowell Post Office Building”.

opus.w: This section only names a Post Office building and says that references to it in federal records use the new name. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, placed on an advisory body or granted a right to sue. The word "regulation" appears only in the references clause, which does not give any agency power to issue rules, so it is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The references clause mentions a "regulation," which could look like rulemaking. That fails because the clause only says that existing mentions of the building in federal records now refer to the new name. It gives no agency power to issue rules, and no one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or allowed to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section simply designates a specific USPS facility with a name and mandates that references to the facility use that name. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this designation. The action is unilateral and administrative.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision. The section is purely declarative, establishing a name and how it should be referenced. There is no mention of hearings, comments, advisory boards, or consultations with non-federal entities.
